sources.title: Neil Armstrong Hall of Engineering
sources.provider: Purdue University official BuildingShapesZip4 ArcGIS FeatureServer
sources.method: Converted feature vertices from Web Mercator to lon/lat, then Purdue project local tangent approximation; subtracted manifest placement marker (-109.0, 400.1893310547), zero marker rotation. Area computed after local projection.
sources.uncertainty: Building polygon supports a ground footprint boundary. It does not define facade wall lines, courtyard voids, upper-floor plans, or exact entrance position. Used only as a thin ground-level plate, not extruded walls.

sources.title: Neil Armstrong Hall of Engineering structural project description
sources.source_date: Project completed 2006; source page current at retrieval
sources.crs: Not applicable; project description and photographs
evidence: Three-story cast-in-place frame with steel mechanical penthouse and basement/partial sub-basement.
Exposed concrete bridge at two levels through atrium and three concrete stairs.
sources.method: Used to relabel/reposition existing model slabs as two atrium bridge levels and to guide source-supported massing/roof interpretation. Bridge positions, routes and stair locations remain schematic; page provides no dimensioned plan.

sources.title: Neil Armstrong Hall of Engineering case history
sources.provider: Design and Build With Metal / Arconic
evidence: High roof described as a warped wing-like cantilever on both ends, clad in Mayflower Red ACM.
Atrium ceiling described as 53 feet high.
Canopy/vestibule clad in Sea Wolf ACM.
sources.method: Roof slab mesh reshaped to qualitative tapered/warped wing profile with restrained edge lift and small illustrative overhang; exact curvature/overhang is not measured. R1 53 ft atrium datum and materials preserved.

sources.title: 3D anamorphic video wall features Purdue’s most consequential engineers

sources.title: Neil A. Armstrong Papers finding aid, MSA 5
sources.provider: Purdue University Libraries Karnes Archives and Special Collections
sources.source_date: Finding aid revised 2017-08-15; Box 348 item refers to September 2004
evidence: The finding aid lists “Neil Armstrong Hall of Engineering, Purdue University,” development plans, September 2004, Box 348, item 5 (PDF page 303).
sources.method_and_uncertainty: This confirms a relevant archival plan set exists, but the finding aid does not include the drawings. No measured plan or elevation was available to this revision; request/inspect the physical or digitized Box 348 item before changing wall outlines, upper floor plates, or roof curvature.

sources.title: Indiana Current Imagery ImageServer; catalog item in2023_29971887_06
sources.provider: Indiana Geographic Information Office (IGIO), DynamicWebMercator ImageServer
sources.pixel_size: 06 in. (0.5 ft; catalog reports HighPS 0.3048 m and LowPS 0.1524 m)
sources.method: Queried the official catalog at the GIS footprint extent. Requested a 2000 x 900 pixel export in EPSG:3857 over bbox [-9675473.17973648,4928688.31898462,-9675190.20021127,4928833.11569478]. Reprojected the GIS ring and source shell wall-edge vertices through the documented Purdue local-frame transform into this raster extent. The composite is a plan-registration comparison only.
evidence: The source is a single connected campus building polygon (FID 642), rather than a bundle of separate feature polygons.

The orthophoto depicts an expansive connected building with multiple roof/wall volumes around an atrium/courtyard; this supports the interpretation that the GIS outline covers wings absent from the current shell-wall model.
Existing shell wall extents are materially narrower in depth and shorter overall than the full GIS footprint.
sources.uncertainty: The dataset is orthophoto imagery but roof/cantilever overhang and elevated surfaces may lean or displace relative to ground-wall boundaries. The image can establish identity and broad envelope composition, not exact interior division, floor-plan geometry, wall elevations, or roof-truss section. The 2023 imagery predates current changes and does not establish current interior exhibits.

r2_changes.change: Added GIS-traced thin base footprint to existing atrium floor mesh.
r2_changes.basis: Official feature 642 footprint and manifest marker transform.
r2_changes.uncertainty: Ground footprint polygon only; no claims about wall lines, holes, or upper levels.

r2_changes.change: Repositioned existing two slabs/rails toward atrium center to represent the structural source’s two exposed bridge levels.
r2_changes.basis: Structural engineer page says exposed concrete bridge at two levels through atrium.
r2_changes.uncertainty: Exact bridge route/coordinates unsupported; current centerline is a renderable schematic.

r2_changes.change: Rebuilt existing red roof slab meshes as tapered, warped winglike surfaces.
r2_changes.basis: Project case history and 2007 building photos identify a winglike cantilever roof.
r2_changes.uncertainty: Exact roof curvature, tip shape, and overhang are not dimensioned; modeled profile is qualitative.

validation: See validation_r2.json. Individual asset saved and reopened before validation and renders. Master file and shared project files were not written.

r3_changes.change: Added an official 2023 Indiana orthophoto tile source snapshot, catalog provenance, and a georeferenced comparison plate overlaying Purdue GIS FID 642 and the saved shell-wall edges.
r3_changes.basis: Indiana Geographic Information Office ImageServer catalog identifies tile in2023_29971887_06 as Image_Year 2023, Tippecanoe County, 06 in pixel size; catalog item intersects the building extent. GIS FID 642 and shell wall edges were projected into the image extent without moving geometry.
r3_changes.result: The GIS feature is one contiguous building footprint polygon, not a set of separate GIS features. The imagery shows a broad connected, multi-wing building composition and an open courtyard/atrium relationship. Existing modeled structural wall edges occupy only the central narrow bar, with extents 126.0 x 26.5 m versus GIS 162.3 x 56.8 m. This indicates omitted plan coverage rather than an obvious separate-volume or canopy-only feature.
r3_changes.uncertainty: The imagery is an aerial raster with visible elevated roof/cantilever surfaces. Roof edges and pixel positions cannot be treated as exact ground-wall corners. GIS supports footprint coverage only; it does not resolve internal wall lines, separate wing boundaries, exact courtyard limits, floor-by-floor plans, or elevations. No geometry was stretched or extruded in R3.

r3_changes.change: No edits were made to the saved Blender asset in R3.
r3_changes.basis: The orthophoto/GIS comparison establishes a substantive plan mismatch but not reliable vertical wall heights, roof elevations, floor/bridge placement, or the exact architectural breakdown of the polygon.
r3_changes.uncertainty: A registered architectural plan/elevation or survey is still needed before adding the missing wing geometry with defensible floor heights and atrium openings.

r3_geometry_decision: No source-backed vertical geometry change was made. Current orthophoto plus GIS confirms that the R2 shell omits broad building wings; the imagery does not provide dimensioned wall/elevation/atrium data to safely build those volumes. Preserve the mismatch as unresolved pending the 2004 development plan drawings or a registered as-built survey.
